This is what & workers have been telling people all along. When I moved to Chicago well after the 2008 recession, I could find jobs, but they only paid $11/hour - not enough to live off.

. . . no social life (no bars or restaurants); no travel (even to see family); no retirement savings; no paying off student loans; credit card charges to plug the gaps; no healthcare (had insurance, but what if the doctor diagnosed something I couldn't afford to treat?)

And $15 is the floor for survival - we didn't live large & it was just enough to pay the bills with $0 extra. That meant no Christmas or birthday presents; no food from restaurants; bus rides that were over an hour to work with an outdoor transfer in Chicago winters . . .
